The numbers

"At the sell window" is the clean test of the alts themselves: value in BTC on the day the window opens, before anything is sold at the top. "End" also includes the top sale and bear rebuy.

Does selling alts on the way up help?

Each cell: sell this share of an alt every time it gains this much, then buy BTC after a 10% BTC pullback. Blue beats never selling (the outlined cell), orange loses to it.

When should you buy the alts?

Same basket (the five largest alts on the day you buy), held without selling until the sell window, then everything sold at the top. Scored in BTC on the day the window opens, from 1 BTC. Above 1.00 means the alts beat simply holding BTC.

Basket Lab

Build your own five-alt basket

Pick any five alts that ranked in the top 200. Each is run through the plan: 1 BTC bought in four slices (the halving, +60, +120, +180 days), held without selling, sold in the sell window, and rebought as BTC in the bear. A coin that wasn't trading yet on a buy date keeps that slice in BTC.

Picking coins by looking at what already happened is the easiest way to fool yourself. Trust a basket that holds up in every cycle and beats most random baskets, not one big number.

"Random baskets": 1,000 random five-coin baskets drawn from the top 20 on that halving date, scored the same way. The percentile is where your basket lands, measured when the sell window opens.

The math of selling on fixed gains

An alt runs up and later falls back. Selling a share at every step locks in gains but leaves less of the position for the rest of the run. Move the sliders to see which one wins.
